For the Hanover specific (non-ISO) programs that do not have a PMF, we used proxy PMFs as shown above.
PMF Changes were based on indicated rate need, as well as the historical performance of specific programs. For example, a program with a higher loss ratio may warrant a PMF increase while a program with a low or steady loss ratio may warrant a PMF 
decrease or no change at all. Another factor considered in implementing PMF changes was the corresponding ISO PMF for that program (if applicable). As we believe ISO's factors to be adequate, we try to move our PMF's toward ISO gradually so not too 
cause too much policyholder disruption.
